programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Murder By Mail: Keith Cottingham
programmes.d: In 1984 a parcel bomb was sent to a 53-year-old grandmother living in a tranquil English village. She died of horrific injuries. No one understood why it had happened. The only evidence detectives had was the bomb itself.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Hitman And The Hairdresser: Fadi Nasri
programmes.d: A 29-year-old hairdresser was found brutally stabbed on her doorstep in a quiet suburban street of London. A recording of a threatening phone call seemed to suggest the motive, but every lead comes to a dead end.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: DNA Of A Murder: Andrew George
programmes.d: Hilda Murrell, a 78-year-old distinguished rose-grower, was found dead in woodland near her home town. Despite a huge investigation by the British police, detectives failed to find her killer and conspiracy theories muddied the waters still further.

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Stephen Port was convicted of the assaults, rapes and murders of Anthony Walgate, Gabriel Kovari, Daniel Whitworth and Jack Taylor. He was sentenced to life imprisonment with a whole life order.

programmes.t: Killer Britain

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Dermot Murnaghan remembers the morning of 2 June 2010 when the news broke of a gunman on the loose in Cumbria, indiscriminately killing strangers. Along with former Met detective Clive Driscoll, Dermot looks back on the remarkable events of that day.

programmes.t: Killer Britain

programmes.t: Killer Britain
programmes.d: Dermot Murnaghan looks back on the disturbing tale of how a sadistic game played by Isabella Gossling and her boyfriend Richard Moors resulted in the death of an innocent young man.

programmes.t: Killer Britain: Vincent Tabak
programmes.d: When landscape architect Joanna Yeates disappeared after work Christmas drinks, the nation was gripped by the search for her. Tragedy struck on Christmas day morning when her body was found in a snow-covered lane. But who had killed the young woman

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos
programmes.d: Mark Howe, an avid viewer of the US series Dexter, stabbed his mother 53 times with a 12-inch knife after an argument about his cannabis use.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos
programmes.d: The ‘Black Widower’ Malcolm Webster was a serial seducer who married three different women. The episode focuses on wife Claire, who Webster murdered in 1994, drugging and setting fire to the car she was in to fake a fatal car crash.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos
programmes.d: Gareth MacDonald was brutally killed by his lover, conman Glenn Rycroft, at a Travelodge on the way to London.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Teenage Son Groomed Online And Lured To His Death - Breck Bednar
programmes.d: Lewis Daynes lured 14-year-old Breck Bednar to his flat after grooming him over the internet for several months. He used duct tape to bind his young victim’s wrists and ankles before slashing his throat in a sadistic attack.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Son In Law Burnt My Family To Death - Melissa Crook
programmes.d: In the early hours of September 10, 2011, Danai Muhammadi and an accomplice used a garden spray to start a blaze that killed his estranged wife Melissa Crook, his father-in-law Mark Crook and his own baby, 15-month-old Noah Crook.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Disabled Daughter Tortured And Murdered By Her Friends - Gemma Hayter
programmes.d: Former Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny examine Gemma Hayter’s child-like trust in people and look at chilling CCTV recordings that show her being led to her death.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: Our Daughter Murdered In Snuff Movie Fantasy - Georgia Williams
programmes.d: Former Detective Superintendent David Swindle and psychologist Emma Kenny give us an insight into Jamie Reynolds’ twisted mind and reveal the full extent of his morbid fascination with extreme violence against women.

programmes.t: Britain's Darkest Taboos: My Daughter Stalked, Then Murdered By Her Ex - Rana Faruqui
programmes.d: Rana Faruqui’s former boyfriend Stephen Griffiths refused to accept that their relationship, which had only lasted a few months, was over and that Rana wanted nothing more to do with him.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Christopher Foster
programmes.d: Failed businessman Christopher Foster killed his wife and daughter before burning their mansion in Shropshire to the ground in August 2008.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: The Marchioness Disaster
programmes.d: The story of the Marchioness; a pleasure boat that collided with dredger Bowbelle and sank within minutes resulting in the loss of 51 lives.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Clare Wood
programmes.d: In April 2007, Clare Wood met George Appleton on a dating website and they embarked on a relationship together. Unbeknownst to her, Appleton was a criminal with a severe history of violence against women.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Suzy Lamplugh
programmes.d: A look at the case of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh, who showed a client around a house in Fulham in July 1986 and was never seen again. Dermot Murnaghan hosts.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Manchester
programmes.d: The series returns to take a closer look at the most horrific crimes ever committed on British soil, starting with the May 2017 Manchester Arena bombing.

programmes.t: Crimes That Shook Britain: Ann Maguire
programmes.d: The tragic story of Ann Maguire, who was stabbed to death by a teenage pupil while teaching a Spanish lesson at Corpus Christi Catholic College in Leeds.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: The Body In The Suitcase: Lorenzo Simon
programmes.d: On 12th May 2014 a human torso was discovered in a suitcase during routine maintenance work on a Birmingham canal. With no useable DNA and no other body parts, the case initially seemed impossible to crack.

programmes.t: Robbie Coltrane's Critical Evidence: Little Miss Nobody: Alan Charlton
programmes.d: An old carpet dug up by workmen in a Cardiff back garden in 1989 was the beginning of a case that would push the boundaries of forensic science. The carpet contained human bones - but whose?
